label: Observed AP count
definition: Number of access points retained in the query RSS feature vector.
details: The count measures scan visibility, not the number of installed or discovered access points. AP labels remain unit-local.

label: RSS standard deviation
definition: Population standard deviation across all RSS observations in the current query.
details: A wide RSS distribution is not necessarily harmful; the prespecified direction did not remain consistent across evaluation conditions.

label: RSS range
definition: Difference between strongest and weakest recorded RSS in a query.
details: The range summarizes signal-strength dispersion; it is not directly a measure of positioning error.

label: Nearest RSS-template distance
definition: Smallest normalized Euclidean distance from the query RSS vector to a reference template.
details: Missing AP features are filled at −110 dBm in the native computation. Training scans at the same reference coordinate/floor are averaged into a template.

label: Nearest-match isolation
definition: Relative separation of the first two nearest RSS-template distances.
details: A larger gap makes the nearest RSS template more distinguishable from the runner-up, but does not independently establish positioning accuracy.

label: Nearest-template cosine similarity
definition: Cosine similarity between the query and its nearest RSS template after offsetting each vector by the RSS floor.
details: A result is unavailable when the shifted vector norm is zero. The display illustrates a vector-angle comparison; per-AP template RSS values are not included in the browser sample.

label: Maximum AP-set overlap
definition: Largest Jaccard agreement between the observed query AP set and one of the ten retrieved reference-template AP sets.
details: The reference AP set is the union of observed APs from scans aggregated into the template.

label: Mean AP-set overlap
definition: Mean Jaccard agreement between query APs and the ten retrieved templates.
details: Unlike maximum overlap, this describes the whole retrieved candidate group.

label: AP-set novelty
definition: Complement of the maximum query-to-template AP-set overlap.
details: Novelty increases as the query AP set becomes less compatible with the best reference template.

label: Nearest reference-point distance
definition: Distance between an estimator-produced position and the closest radio-map reference point.
details: Estimator-specific. Unlike the other examples, it requires a separately generated predicted position; no estimator prediction is supplied by this browser-only atlas.

label: Local reference-point density
definition: Number of distinct training reference coordinates within an adaptive radius around the candidate centroid.
details: The radius is r = clip(3 × median positive nearest-neighbor spacing, 2 m, 25 m); default 5 m if the spacing cannot be resolved. The live candidate plot shows only the top ten, not every RP counted.

label: Candidate spatial spread
definition: Root mean squared spatial distance of the ten retrieved reference coordinates from their centroid.
details: A high value indicates retrieved fingerprints spread across local coordinates. Floor categories are not added as a vertical metric in this 2D calculation.

label: Candidate-set diameter
definition: Largest pairwise 2D separation among the ten retrieved reference coordinates.
details: Highlights distant outlying candidate references even if most candidates are clustered.

label: Cumulative-neighborhood instability
definition: Maximum displacement between a cumulative rank-k candidate centroid and the final ten-candidate centroid.
details: Ordered by RSS-template similarity. This is a diagnostic of rank-dependent spatial stability, not a time-series displacement.

label: RSS-gradient uncertainty proxy
definition: Candidate spatial spread divided by the RSS-distance contrast across ranks 1–10.
details: Large spatial spread with a narrow RSS-distance range indicates spatial ambiguity relative to signal-space separation.

label: Scan Quality and Support Score (SQS)
definition: Equal-weight average of signal-match, candidate-geometry, AP-count, overlap and local-density support.
details: R(z) is 5th–95th percentile clipped scaling within the full evaluation unit. Missing component values are omitted from the mean. SQS is not a calibrated probability.

label: Signal-to-spread support (Cσ)
definition: Signal-match support reduced by normalized candidate spread.
details: The denominator penalizes diffuse spatial candidate sets while preserving the normalized RSS-match numerator.

label: Fingerprint Integrity Index (FII)
definition: Average of signal support, AP count, maximum overlap, match isolation and inverse AP novelty.
details: Five component terms are unit-relative. FII and SQS use different component definitions and cannot be interpreted as interchangeable probabilities.
